why: Owner on /kit/interval-track: 'still not the biggest fan of the blue and the text colour choices, maybe review that component again', 'hovering and focus also a bit weird'. Span fills come from series registration (charts/parts/interval-track.tsx:432-440 via parts/cartesian-adapt.ts:37), so a one-series track is a wall of full-strength brand blue. Label ink is picked by position, not by contrast (interval-track.tsx:557-563): card-surface ink inside a solid span, the series colour on a back layer, muted ink elsewhere. Hover draws a brand ring rect on the span (:463) and a surface veil over all others (:450-456), which reads as the chart blinking.
owns: packages/basalt-ui/src/charts/core/theme.ts (only for a token the track needs)
must_not_touch: apps/playground/src/scenarios/expr/** and apps/playground/src/cycle/** (trial builds are never hand-finished; v3-owner-2-rerun rebuilds them)
change: Spec with shots, light and dark, three variants side by side on the same week: the present one and two quieter ones. Aim: a span is a tinted block with a stronger leading edge or a soft fill with full-ink text, colour carries a category only when there is more than one, and a single-series track is neutral with the accent kept for the focused or current span. Label ink meets contrast against its own fill by derivation, not by position. Hover: the hovered span gets a small lift (stroke or tone), the others keep their paint; no veil unless a selection is held. Take the owner's verdict, build the chosen variant, remove the others.
acceptance: A Spec with three variants in light and dark has a verdict before code merges
Every label passes the kit's contrast check against its fill in both schemes (test)
A hover changes paint on the hovered span only (test)
A one-series track uses no brand fill at rest
commits: feat: the look with its test (package); chore: the playground page.
note: Source: the owner's second hands-on review of the v3 playground on 2026-11-19, after owner review 1 merged. He asked again for the cause to be fixed, not the page he named.
